turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, sorry we are a bit late. I had to bring him myself. He will say he is fine, but he is not fine only.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): I am fine. Why you dragged me in this heat? I was resting. This whole visit is unnecessary.
[SEG0003] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mr Iyer, I am Dr Mehta. You are seventy-four, yes? Please sit, both of you. Your wife has concerns about memory, and I want your version also, not only hers.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): My version is there is no problem. She worries for everything. Even the milk she checks twice.

[SEG0005] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Since two-three months he asks the same thing again and again. This morning, four times, did you book the gas cylinder. And he is forgetting appointments. The dentist last month, and the eye check, both he missed.

[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): I did not miss anything. The dentist himself phoned and cancelled. The eye check I never agreed to. And I don't repeat questions. You don't listen the first time, that is all.

[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me say it back. From you, Mrs Iyer, repeating questions and missed appointments over two-three months. From you, Mr Iyer, those things did not happen. Did he lose his way outside at any time?

[SEG0008] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yes. He went to the vegetable market and got lost coming back. Nearly two hours, and our neighbour brought him to the gate. I think it was Thursday. Or, well, actually, maybe the week before. I cannot fix the date.
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Lost? Rubbish. I knew the road. Tomatoes were forty rupees, too much, so I walked around. Crowded only, and I took the long way by the temple.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): I had asked about losing the way, not the price of tomatoes. We can leave the market rates.
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Hmm. You are also going on and on. I am tired. My legs are feeling heavy. Can we go home?
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): We will note the tiredness and the heavy legs. Any falls in the last month?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Those waiting chairs are a punishment. My back is paining from sitting there. And the fan is making a racket. Nobody oils it.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): I am sorry the chairs were bad. I was asking something else. Have you actually fallen, on the ground, recently?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I have not fallen. What a question.
[SEG0016] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No falls, I would have known. But he should not be going out alone now. That is my fear.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): How long do you yourself think the forgetting has been going on?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): If you insist on calling it forgetting, five-ish years. Old age, keys, spectacles. Everyone in our building is the same.
[SEG0019] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No, doctor, not five years. This change is two-three months only. Before that he was doing the bank papers and the bills himself.

[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Alright, I will say it back. One of you puts it around five years, the other at two or three months. You have not agreed, so I am keeping a range, roughly a couple of months up to about five years, not a fixed figure.
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Write whatever you like. I want to finish.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any headache, fever, or weakness of one side of the body?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): No headache. No fever. Both hands are working, see, I am lifting them. Don't add diseases.
[SEG0024] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No fever at home either. He eats less, but that is not new.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): Chest pain, or breathlessness on walking?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): The chemist near the signal has shifted, that is why last week the strips came late. Very inconvenient.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): That is a different point, we can park it. Any pain in the chest, or shortness of breath?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): No chest pain. Breathing is fine. I walked up, didn't I?
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Urine, motions, any change there?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): All normal. You want to send me to every room or what?
[SEG0031] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Urine and bowels are normal. Sleep is the thing, broken. He wakes around three and asks me what time it is, as if he did not ask yesterday.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): I wake because you snore, not because of any sleep problem. Don't make a diagnosis out of snoring.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): Noted, you disagree on the sleep. Old illnesses now. Diabetes and blood pressure, still with him?
[SEG0034] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yes, both ongoing. Sugar for ten years, BP for fifteen years. The tablets I keep in one dabba. He cannot tell you which strip is which.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): I can tell. I am sitting here only. Don't speak as if I have left the room.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): Diabetes and high blood pressure, long standing, yes, I have that. Any operations in the past?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Cataract, both eyes, some years back. Nothing else. No heart surgery, no hernia, nothing.
[SEG0038] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yes, both cataracts, a few years ago. That is the only surgery.
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): In the family, sugar or memory trouble in the parents?
[SEG0040] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): His mother had diabetes. Father was clear in the head till the end, that much I know.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Mother had sugar, correct. Father was sharp. No need to dig more.
[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): Smoking, alcohol?
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Never smoked in my life. Alcohol I left years back. Nothing now. Tea only, too much tea maybe.

[SEG0044] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Never smoked, that is true. We live together, our flat in Chembur. He retired from the bank, clerical side, about ten years back. He still tries to go to the market alone.
[SEG0045] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thank you. Medicines, since you manage them. Please list what he actually takes these days.

[SEG0046] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Amlodipine five milligram, one tablet in the morning, for the BP. Metformin five hundred milligram morning and night, for the sugar. Atorvastatin twenty milligram at night, for cholesterol. I give the morning ones with water after brushing, and the statin after dinner.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): Amlodipine is ten milligram, not five. I saw the strip. You are saying five from an old habit.
[SEG0048] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It is five milligram, Ramesh. Well, actually the ten was years ago, the doctor changed it. You are remembering the old strip. I give five.
[SEG0049] person_2 (PATIENT): Ten. I am not a fool.

[SEG0050] person_3 (DOCTOR): I will not, um, choose between five and ten sitting here. You differ, so the amlodipine dose stays unsettled until the strips are in front of me. Metformin five hundred morning and night, and atorvastatin twenty at night, those two, any quarrel?
[SEG0051] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Those two are correct. Only, the night metformin he misses sometimes. He tells me he already took it, and the tablet is still in the dabba.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): I take it when I remember. Most nights it goes in. Some nights, um, maybe not. What to do.
[SEG0053] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): There is also a small white tablet for acidity, when the burning starts. Round one. I have forgotten the name completely. The chemist packed it loose.
[SEG0054] person_3 (DOCTOR): Then we record a small white tablet for acidity, name unknown, only when there is burning. Any allergy, medicines, food, anything?
[SEG0055] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No allergy. I can eat what I want. Nothing happens.
[SEG0056] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Penicillin he should not take. Years ago a rash came all over the body after penicillin. We have avoided it from that time.
[SEG0057] person_2 (PATIENT): That was heat rash in summer, not penicillin. I have no allergy to penicillin. No allergy to anything.

[SEG0058] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me say it back so I don't muddle it. You, Mr Iyer, report no allergies at all. Your wife reports a penicillin rash and avoidance since. You disagree, so I will not mark it as a confirmed allergy, and I am not challenging you with a test today.
[SEG0059] person_2 (PATIENT): Good. Then finish. I am tired of this chair also.

[SEG0060] person_3 (DOCTOR): One minute, I will examine. Pulse is regular, seventy-six per minute. Chest is clear, no added sounds. No swelling around the ankles. You gave the weekday right, Wednesday, but the date was off, you said the twelfth and today is the nineteenth.
[SEG0061] person_2 (PATIENT): You mixed me up with too many questions. I know Wednesday. Dates I don't chase.

[SEG0062] person_3 (DOCTOR): I am not putting any diagnosis on this today. I will not name it. I want blood tests for things we might still treat, full blood count, HbA1c, thyroid function, vitamin B12, and kidney function, and I will send you for a memory assessment.
[SEG0063] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Memory assessment, meaning MRI or what?

[SEG0064] person_3 (DOCTOR): No scan from me today. A memory clinic assessment. The blood tests I am arranging now. Please bring every strip next visit, especially amlodipine, so five or ten can be settled.
[SEG0065] person_2 (PATIENT): More tests. I told you I am fine. Nobody hears the patient.

[SEG0066] person_3 (DOCTOR): I do hear you. Even so, the bloods are booked and the memory assessment referral is going through. Till then, please do not go out alone, and let your wife keep charge of the tablets.
[SEG0067] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I will keep the dabba. For the market, I will go with him. He won't like it, but okay.
[SEG0068] person_2 (PATIENT): I am not a schoolchild to be escorted.

[SEG0069] person_3 (DOCTOR): If he gets lost again, or there is sudden drowsiness, or weakness of one side, don't wait for me, come straight away. Otherwise I will see both of you in six weeks, with the results.
[SEG0070] person_2 (PATIENT): Six weeks in that same chair. Wonderful.
[SEG0071] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): One more thing, his weight. He keeps saying seventy-two kilos. On the clinic scale last month it was sixty-eight. I don't know which one you want.
[SEG0072] person_2 (PATIENT): Seventy-two. Their scale is ancient. Mine is from the gym, it is correct.

[SEG0073] person_3 (DOCTOR): Weight also is disputed, seventy-two from you, sixty-eight from the clinic scale your wife remembers. I have not weighed you today, so I will not force one number. We can stop. Go home safely, and bring the strips.

spec.situation: Spouse brings an older person who 'is fine' but repeats questions, forgets appointments and got lost; patient disagrees on many points; medicines managed by spouse; doctor plans bloods and a memory assessment, no diagnosis said aloud.
features: disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.
patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.

spoken_numbers: doses, vitals and durations are spoken as words or sloppy speech ('a hundred and two point five', 'one-forty over ninety', 'five-ish years', 'twenty milligram'); the label writes them normally (102.5, 140/90, 20 mg) and does not turn vague ones into exact ones.
relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.

bad.reason: Forgetfulness and disputed duration range supported; reported_by is not only family member.
bad.text: Forgetfulness (category=neurological, status=present, duration=approximately 2 months to 5 years, temporality=current, reported_by=family_member, certainty=certain)

bad.reason: Family member says he eats less, but also says it is not new.

omissions.text: Amlodipine dose is explicitly disputed: wife reports 5 mg each morning, patient says 10 mg, and the doctor left the dose unsettled until the strips are checked. Recording amlodipine without this unresolved dose in the medication entry is incomplete.
Metformin adherence issue: wife reports he sometimes misses the night 500 mg dose, and patient agrees that some nights he may not take it.
The doctor specifically stated no diagnosis is being made today and would not name it.
Family history also included that the father had no memory trouble / was clear in the head till the end.
The doctor clarified that the planned memory assessment is a memory clinic assessment and that no scan/MRI is being ordered today.
Blood tests were not just planned but booked/being arranged now.
